record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Endemic-equilibrium existence and uniqueness for SIR-PH variants
record.original_question: Consider deterministic epidemic models with standard incidence and linear birth rate b(N)=Lambda N, one susceptible compartment S, one removed or immunized compartment R, and an n-dimensional vector I of disease compartments. In the SIR-PH class, disease-state transitions are encoded by a matrix A, infection forces by a matrix B, disease-induced mortality by a vector delta, loss of immunity by gamma_r, and vaccination by gamma_s. The first approximation SIR-PH-FA drops the quadratic fatality terms in the scaled equations, while the intermediate approximation SIR-PH-IA keeps the fatality terms in the susceptible and removed equations but not in the infectious equations. For the scaled SIR-PH, SIR-PH-FA, and SIR-PH-IA classes, does the condition R0>1 always imply that there is exactly one biologically feasible endemic equilibrium with positive disease components?

evidence.quote: Our paper presents three new classes of models: SIR-PH, SIR-PH-FA, and SIR-PH-IA, and states two problems we would like to solve about them.

However, it is quite common that
1. When R0 > 1, there exists a unique fixed endemic point, and
2. the endemic point is locally stable when R0 > 1.

The model (3.5) with Φs = Φi = Φr = 1 will be called scaled model (SM ).
2. The model (3.5) with Φs = Φi = Φr = 0 will be called first approximation (FA ).
3. The model (3.5) with Φs = Φr = 1, Φi = 0 will be called intermediate approximation (IA ).

Remark 13 A yet another open problem is whether the endemic point must always exists for the FA and
IA models.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider deterministic compartmental epidemic models with standard incidence, a linear birth term b(N)=Λ N (Λ>0), one susceptible compartment S, one removed/immunized compartment R, and an n-dimensional vector I=(I_1,…,I_n) of disease compartments. The dynamics in the SIR-PH framework are specified by:

• a sub-generator matrix A∈ℝ^{n×n} (the PH transition matrix between infectious phases, with A1≤0),
• a nonnegative matrix B∈ℝ^{n×n} encoding the forces of infection generated by each infectious phase,
• a nonnegative vector δ∈ℝ^n of disease-induced mortality rates,
• constants γ_r≥0 (loss of immunity rate) and γ_s≥0 (vaccination rate from S to R),
• a probability vector α (initial distribution among infectious phases at infection).

Writing N=S+R+1·I and scaling variables (s,i,r)=(S/N,I/N,R/N), one obtains a system of ODEs of the form (3.5):

ds/dt = Λ(1−s) − s(αᵀ·B i) + γ_r r − γ_s s + Φ_s · s(δᵀ i),
di/dt = α s(αᵀ·B i) (rewriting with B) + Aᵀ i − Λ i + Φ_i · i(δᵀ i) − δ∘i terms,
dr/dt = γ_s s − γ_r r − Λ r − (−A1)ᵀ_recov i + Φ_r · r(δᵀ i),

where Φ_s,Φ_i,Φ_r∈{0,1} are switches. Define three submodels:
(SM) scaled model: Φ_s=Φ_i=Φ_r=1,
(FA) first approximation: Φ_s=Φ_i=Φ_r=0,
(IA) intermediate approximation: Φ_s=Φ_r=1, Φ_i=0.

Let R_0 denote the basic reproduction number computed by the next-generation method from this system. A biologically feasible endemic equilibrium is a fixed point (s*,i*,r*) of the chosen submodel with s*,r*≥0, i*>0 componentwise, and s*+r*+1·i*≤1 (or =1 after scaling).

Question. For each of the three classes SM, FA, and IA, does the condition R_0>1 always imply the existence and uniqueness of a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium with positive disease components, for every admissible choice of parameters (Λ, A, B, δ, γ_r, γ_s, α) and every dimension n≥1?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem in the work introducing the SIR-PH, SIR-PH-FA, and SIR-PH-IA classes. While explicit candidate formulas for an endemic point in the FA class exist, its always-belonging to the biologically feasible domain has not been established, and uniqueness/existence in general for SM and IA remains unresolved. No subsequent published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: New Results and Open Questions for SIR-PH Epidemic Models (MDPI Symmetry)
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit endemic point formulas are available for SIR-PH-FA, but it remains to verify it always lies in the invariant domain; the authors could not establish this in general.
status_evidence.claim: Existence/uniqueness of a feasible endemic equilibrium under R0>1 for the SIR-PH families is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2205.03700
status_evidence.snippet: Remark: a yet another open problem is whether the endemic point must always exist for the FA and IA models.
status_evidence.claim: Open problem explicitly listed for FA and IA submodels.
